relation: two distinct contracts: uniform excluded-minor witness alone (X192), or witness AND ordinary minor closure (X168)
summary: C11 preserves two intentional representation contracts under one dependency-coupled family. X192 aliases excludes_a_minor ONLY. X168 aliases the explicit conjunction proper_minor_closed_class. Classes are arbitrary sgraph-to-Prop predicates, including the empty class, and the witness is any finite simple graph.

Reuse upstream minor with HOST FIRST, minor_trans, strict_is_minor, iso_strict_minor, induced_minor and small_K_free. minor_self is derived from the identity isomorphism; no nonexistent upstream reflexivity lemma is assumed. Actual minor closure implies C10 iso/induced/strong hereditary closure, but the witness-only interface gains no closure premise.

Freeze both exact helpers and both complete rows. X192 preserves alpha before the class, the triangle-free algorithm domain, output bounds and open/done status. X168 preserves class-uniform K, connected guard and K*(|V|+1), partial/BLOCKED status and the documented extension-complexity vacuity. Blocked edge e161 and all statement documentation remain unchanged.

No pre-existing proof consumer or frozen snapshot reaches either helper. No historical Original is needed. Only the two now-migrated distinct-variant entries are removed from C10 metadata; every earlier frozen body/review field stays unchanged. X198 inline closure without properness, U8 vertex-minor/proper_class and quantitative fixed-H class bounds remain outside scope.

Public-only examples include empty/universal/zero-order classes, a supplied excluded minor, ordinary closure implying strong hereditary closure, and a positive exact-order class that excludes a minor but is not closed under minors. Exact kernel types, all four compatibility iff declarations, strict frozen/live closures and independent step-10/root final review are required.
